pages.x: In 376 tens of thousands of Goths, fleeing the Huns, begged to be let across the Danube into the empire. The Romans let them in, then starved and cheated them: officers traded dogs to eat for their children as slaves, a Roman historian wrote. The Goths rose in revolt.

In 378 the emperor Valens attacked the Goths near Adrianople without waiting for help from the west. The Gothic horsemen came back from foraging and caught his army on a hot August afternoon. Two thirds of it was destroyed, and Valens was never found.

In 410 Alaric, king of the Visigoths, tired of waiting for the land and pay he had been promised, took and plundered Rome itself, the first time in 800 years an enemy had done so. He spared the churches. The whole Roman world was stunned.

In the 440s Attila ruled an empire from the Rhine to the Black Sea and made Constantinople pay him tonnes of gold. In 451 Romans and Goths together stopped him in Gaul, at the Catalaunian Plains. He invaded Italy the next year but turned back, and died in 453.

The Vandals crossed from Spain to Africa in 429 and took Carthage and the rich grain lands that fed Rome. In 455 their king Gaiseric sailed to Rome and plundered it for two weeks. That is why wrecking things is still called vandalism.

By now the western emperors were puppets of Germanic generals. In 476 one of them, Odoacer, removed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus, sent him to live on an estate near Naples, and sent the imperial robes to Constantinople: the west no longer needed an emperor of its own.

A German historian once counted 210 reasons that have been given, from lead pipes to Christianity. Most historians now point to civil wars between generals, an empire split in two whose richer eastern half stayed safe, money troubles, and peoples on the move whom Rome could no longer beat or take in.

The west broke up into kingdoms of Goths, Franks, Vandals and others that grew into the countries of Europe. But Rome did not vanish: its eastern half lasted another thousand years, and Latin, Roman law and the Church lived on in the west.
pts: The last western emperor removed in 476
